# MySupportInfo

> One Link to Diagnose Any Device. Instant client-side system, browser, network, and bufferbloat latency diagnostics for remote teams, IT helpdesks, and developers with zero tracking.

MySupportInfo is a free, 100% in-browser device diagnostic platform. It allows users, IT technicians, sysadmins, and support teams to inspect comprehensive hardware, browser, and network specifications in under 3 seconds without downloading software, configuring agents, or storing user logs.

## Core Diagnostic Tools
- [System Diagnostics Dashboard](https://mysupportinfo.com/): Instant inspection of browser version, operating system, public IP, screen resolution, WebGL GPU, RAM, WebRTC leaks, and network quality.
- [What Is My Browser](https://mysupportinfo.com/what-is-my-browser): Detects browser engine, exact major and minor version, user agent string, JavaScript status, cookie persistence, and client hints.
- [What Is My IP Address](https://mysupportinfo.com/what-is-my-ip): Dual-stack IPv4 and IPv6 detection, ISP organization name, autonomous system (ASN), approximate geolocation, and WebRTC privacy leak audits.
- [What Is My Screen Resolution](https://mysupportinfo.com/what-is-my-screen-resolution): Physical monitor resolution, active CSS viewport dimensions, device pixel ratio (DPR), color depth, and screen orientation.
- [Bufferbloat Latency Test](https://mysupportinfo.com/bufferbloat): Measures network latency and jitter under heavy loaded download and upload conditions, issuing an official letter grade from A to F.

## Documentation and Help
- [Knowledge Base & FAQ](https://mysupportinfo.com/faq): Answers to common questions regarding device detection, user-agent data, WebRTC leaks, and latency under load.
- [Privacy Policy](https://mysupportinfo.com/privacy): Detailed information on our client-side execution model, zero database storage guarantee, and GDPR/CCPA compliance.
- [Terms of Use](https://mysupportinfo.com/terms): Terms of service, acceptable use guidelines, and official technical contact channels.
